input.step_by_step_reasoning: The whiteboard shows two client actors, a CDN boundary, S3, AppSync, API Gateway, Lambda, SQS and DynamoDB. I kept all nine entities as separate nodes with no fusion; the CDN is not named as an AWS service, so it is mapped to ThirdParty. The transcript describes three flows. Flow 0 is tenant onboarding through the wizard web app: client -> CDN -> AppSync -> Lambda -> SQS fan-out -> Lambda -> DynamoDB. Flow 1 is the third-party reseller (OTA) channel: reseller -> CDN -> API Gateway -> Lambda, with the response returned through the CDN. Flow 2 is the customer website/mobile channel: client -> CDN -> S3 static content -> CDN -> client, then dynamic content via AppSync with direct DynamoDB resolvers. The check-in flow reuses the same AppSync/Lambda/DynamoDB/SQS arrows, so it is recorded in the notes of those edges rather than as extra edges. Self-check: the ledger has 16 visual_connections entries and I emit 16 edges, one per entry with the same direction, including both directions of reversed pairs and both UserConsumerMobile -> CDN entries. No edges were added beyond the ledger.

graph.name: Anchor: Multi-Tenant Serverless Ticketing Platform
graph.notes: Anchor is a ticketing platform for daytime experiences (Statue of Liberty cruises, Niagara Falls, Alcatraz Island, NYC Ferry) with more than 40 tenants, over 20 of them onboarded in the last six months. Fully serverless: CDN in front of S3 static hosting, AppSync GraphQL, a REST API Gateway for third-party resellers, shared Lambdas, SQS for fan-out and deferred processing, and DynamoDB shared tables partitioned by tenant.

nodes.name: Web / Mobile Clients
nodes.notes: Tenants using the onboarding wizard web app, customers buying through the owned website or mobile app, and the check-in mobile application that looks up bookings and scans tickets.

nodes.name: Third-Party Resellers (OTAs)
nodes.notes: Online travel agency resellers such as Expedia, Viator and GetYourGuide that sell the offerings through a third-party API.

nodes.name: CDN
nodes.notes: First hop for every client request. Returns static content from S3 and routes dynamic requests to AppSync or API Gateway.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Bucket serving as an HTTP server for the static website content: event descriptions, pictures and ticket offerings.

nodes.name: AppSync
nodes.notes: GraphQL gateway. Resolvers invoke Lambda; direct DynamoDB resolvers are sometimes used and reused through pipeline resolvers.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Regular REST endpoint implemented for third-party resellers (OTAs).

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Shared functions triggered through AppSync and API Gateway for both tenants and consumers. Fans out to subroutines via SQS and later processes those messages.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Holds fan-out messages for tenant setup and deferred post-check-in work (customer service, post-experience tasks, review-reminder email).

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores all tenant data. Multi-tenancy uses shared tables with a partition key per tenant.

edges.notes: Tenant uses the onboarding wizard web application; the request first hits the CDN.
CDN forwards the request to the AppSync GraphQL gateway. The same path is used for dynamic content and check-in.
AppSync resolvers invoke Lambda to fan out to different subroutines; also processes GraphQL nodes for booking and check-in.
Lambda sends a batch of SQS messages for tenant setup; after check-in it queues post-experience work such as the review-reminder email.
Queued messages are processed later by Lambda.
Lambda interacts with DynamoDB to finish setting up the tenancy; data is partitioned by tenant key.
A reseller (OTA) request first hits the CDN.
CDN routes reseller requests to the REST endpoint on API Gateway.
API Gateway invokes the same Lambdas used by the owned mobile and web channels.
Response returned to the reseller through the CDN.
Customer starts the journey on the owned website or mobile app; the request hits the CDN.
CDN requests static content from the S3 bucket acting as an HTTP server.
S3 returns the static offering content: event descriptions and pictures.
CDN returns the content to the client so the customer can browse and navigate.
Direct DynamoDB resolvers return data to AppSync for dynamic content; reusable through pipeline resolvers.
AppSync returns the dynamic GraphQL response through the CDN.
